text:
maria: morning — first day! I'm trying to ssh to the internal bastion but it's timing out. VPN says connected (OpenVPN). Do new hires need split-tunnel enabled to reach 10.* VPC ranges? Who should I ping to get access?

it-support: welcome @maria! We typically add new hires to the redwood-vpc-access SSO group which pushes the VPC routes. Can you confirm your Okta email and VPN client version?

maria: maria.g@redwood.ai, OpenVPN 2.5.9 on macOS Ventura (M1). I ran `netstat -nr` and don't see 10.0.0.0/8 routes. ping 10.1.2.1 -> request timeout.

sam-eng: @maria try `sudo route -n get 10.1.2.1` and paste the output. Also check `scutil --proxy` for any proxy overrides. If you're on a split-tunnel profile we only push private routes; otherwise IT can flip to full-tunnel temporarily.

maria: here's the `route -n get` output I'm seeing:
```
   route to: 10.1.2.1
destination: 10.1.2.1
       mask: 255.255.255.255
    interface: en0
```

sam-eng: hmm that suggests your machine has no specific route; IT should've pushed `10.0.0.0/8` via tun0. @it-support can you check the push profile for this user?

jordan-sec: tagging sec here — once they accept the Okta invite I'll add them to `redwood-bastion-users`. Note: if corporate split-tunnel policy prevents the route, we can allow SSH to bastion via the public NAT egress IP (we'll whitelist it).

it-support: added maria to `redwood-vpc-access` and triggered a re-provision. You should get an email. Reconnect VPN and try again.

system-bot: maria accepted Okta invitation and was added to redwood-vpc-access

maria: reconnected, now I can `ssh ubuntu@redwood-bastion` — success :tada: Thanks everyone!

ben-oncall: quick FYI — if anyone else hits this, open a ticket with VPN client + macOS version + `route -n get` output so we can triage faster. :+1:
